title: Database and API Fundamentals
learning_outcomes: Explain the main security concern and trust boundary involved in Database and API Fundamentals.
Choose an appropriate defensive control for Database and API Fundamentals and state the assumptions under which it works.

content.intro: This lesson belongs to Module 2: Web and Internet Fundamentals. It builds practical understanding of Database and API Fundamentals with the syllabus subtopics retained below.
content.why_it_matters: Database and API Fundamentals gives you the mental model needed to recognize where a security promise begins and ends. Validate identity with a reviewed authentication design, protect session/token lifecycle and recovery, enforce server-side authorization separately, and test expiry, revocation, and failure paths.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Database and API Fundamentals can be understood through this sequence: Define operation → Authenticate request → Authorize object + field → Bound load + audit. Start with the application asset and trust boundary, state what secure behavior should occur, and identify the evidence that would prove or disprove it.

content_blocks.title: Connect the syllabus subtopics
content_blocks.text: The source curriculum groups this lesson around: 13.1 Relational and non-relational databases; 13.2 Basic CRUD operations; 13.3 REST API concepts; 13.4 API authentication and response structures; 13.5 Trust boundaries between application components. Treat these points as a checklist, not a list to memorize: explain the risk, identify the root cause, select a control, and define a test for that control.

items.title: Scope
items.text: Identify the asset, principal, input, state, or boundary affected. State whether the example is local, owned, or explicitly authorized.

items.title: Control
items.text: Validate identity with a reviewed authentication design, protect session/token lifecycle and recovery, enforce server-side authorization separately, and test expiry, revocation, and failure paths.

items.title: Failure behavior
items.text: Include an invalid, denied, expired, malformed, repeated, or otherwise relevant boundary case. Fail safely without exposing secrets.

items.title: Evidence
items.text: Record expected versus actual behavior, a sanitized request or test result, the root cause, the chosen fix, and the regression test.

content_blocks.title: Safe reference example: Database and API Fundamentals
content_blocks.expected_output: The API review checks identity, object permissions, field permissions, and resource limits independently.
content_blocks.run_instructions: This is a test-case record, not a complete API implementation. Add explicit positive and negative assertions to an isolated test suite.
content_blocks.reset_steps: Use a clean local test account and synthetic data. Reset the test fixture after recording the result; do not include credentials or private data in the course report.

content_blocks.title: Common mistake and recovery
content_blocks.text: Do not confuse an observation with proof or rely on a UI-only restriction. Validate identity with a reviewed authentication design, protect session/token lifecycle and recovery, enforce server-side authorization separately, and test expiry, revocation, and failure paths. If evidence is ambiguous, reduce the test to one condition, inspect the application code/configuration, and repeat only within the permitted scope.

content_blocks.title: Execution and safety boundary
content_blocks.text: The current CodeLeaf playground is an HTML/CSS/JavaScript preview, not a secure runner for arbitrary server code. This example is a static reference unless the run instructions explicitly identify a supported local environment. Use a private local lab or a test system with written authorization; do not test unrelated public systems.

content.task: For “Database and API Fundamentals”, write a short security note or test in a local/owned application. Identify the expected secure behavior, at least one relevant failure case, and the evidence needed to prove the control works.
task_acceptance_criteria: Explain the core rule for Database and API Fundamentals in your own words.
Name the trust boundary and the server-side control or policy that applies.
Specify a repeatable test for expected behavior and a relevant denied/failure path.
Use synthetic data and redact credentials, tokens, and personal information from evidence.
hints: Start by stating the asset, input, actor, or trust boundary and the expected secure behavior.
Change one condition at a time; record expected and actual outcomes with synthetic data.
Check the linked official reference for framework-specific settings and version-dependent behavior.
content.expected_output: A concise control explanation and a sanitized test record showing expected/actual behavior, one failure case, and a regression check.
recap: Database and API Fundamentals is a security boundary/control topic, not a standalone checklist item.
Validate identity with a reviewed authentication design, protect session/token lifecycle and recovery, enforce server-side authorization separately, and test expiry, revocation, and failure paths.
Retest fixes and record sanitized evidence; use only authorized environments.
